grammar.name: Futuro semplice: regular forms
grammar.scope: regular future of -are/-ere/-ire; -care/-gare, -ciare/-giare spellings; future for plans and predictions; present-for-future contrast

chapters.a_plot: The engagement party at Franco's. Everyone has plans for the wedding: Lucia's, Franco's, Chiara's and Samira's. They don't match.
chapters.b_plot: Ben announces a plan of his own: he will start a business. Nobody hears him over the wedding talk.
chapters.arc: Season premiere: the wedding arc and Ben's business arc begin.

title.en: What Will You Do When You Grow Up?

grammar.name: Futuro semplice: irregular forms
grammar.scope: sarò, avrò, andrò, verrò, vorrò, potrò, dovrò, saprò, vedrò, vivrò, farò, dirò, berrò, rimarrò, terrò

chapters.a_plot: Career day at Leo's school: he says he will be 'barista like Dad'. Ben is touched, and worried.
chapters.b_plot: Emma, at the liceo's orientation day, has no idea what she will do. Tommaso already knows: music conservatory.
chapters.runner: Franco predicts every family member's future. Every prediction is terrible.

grammar.name: Future of probability
grammar.scope: future for suppositions about the present (sarà a casa, avrà vent'anni); saranno le otto; contrast with forse / probabilmente

chapters.a_plot: Lucia's son Gennaro was supposed to arrive from London for the engagement, and he isn't answering. Where will he be? Theories multiply at the bar.
chapters.b_plot: A mysterious stranger has been sitting at Bar Tigli every morning for a week, taking notes. A food critic? An inspector? A rival?
chapters.arc: Planted: the stranger is an inspector from the council (it pays off with the E15 permits).

grammar.name: Futuro anteriore
grammar.scope: formation (avrò fatto, sarò arrivato); after quando/appena/dopo che; supposition about the past (avrà dimenticato)

chapters.a_plot: Marchetti gives Chiara the studio's biggest project: a building in Rome. It will mean three days a week away. 'Quando avrò finito, tornerò a casa.'
chapters.b_plot: Gennaro finally arrives: he will have missed the train, lost his phone... he did both. He's charming and chaotic; Franco doesn't approve.

grammar.name: Condizionale presente: full forms and uses
grammar.scope: regular and irregular conditional; advice (dovresti), wishes (vorrei), polite requests, hypothetical opinions (al posto tuo / io farei)

chapters.a_plot: Everyone gives Lucia and Franco advice about the wedding. Ornella would do it 'as it was done once'; Samira would do it bigger; Emma would do it on Instagram.
chapters.b_plot: Ben asks Nadia for advice about his business idea: cooking classes for foreigners, plus American brunch at the bar. She'd say... 'Dovresti fare un business plan.'
chapters.runner: Confetti, the sugared almonds: how many, what colour, why?

grammar.name: Condizionale passato
grammar.scope: formation (avrei fatto, sarei andato); regrets (avrei dovuto), missed opportunities; future in the past as a preview (ha detto che sarebbe venuto)

chapters.a_plot: Chiara accepted the Rome project without talking to Ben. Now she's in Rome and he's alone with the kids, the bar and the new business. 'Avresti dovuto chiedermelo.'
chapters.b_plot: Franco tells Gennaro he should have visited his mother more often. Gennaro tells Franco he should have mentioned he was dating his mother.

grammar.name: Relative pronouns: il quale, ciò che, quello che, chi
grammar.scope: il quale/la quale/i quali/le quali; ciò che / quello che; chi (whoever, he who); tutto ciò che

chapters.a_plot: The venue hunt: villas, restaurants, a hall. Nothing is 'ciò che vogliamo'. Then Leo asks: 'Why not the orto?'
chapters.b_plot: Ben looks for 'the right place' for his cooking classes. The bar's kitchen is too small; the Centro civico has rules; Roberto has more rules.
chapters.arc: Decision: the reception will be held in Franco's orto.

grammar.name: Trapassato prossimo
grammar.scope: formation (avevo fatto, ero andato); an action before another past action; già/mai/appena with trapassato

chapters.theme: Family pasts, backstory, divorce and second chances
chapters.a_plot: Gennaro tells Chiara what Lucia had gone through before she met Franco: the divorce, the years alone in Milan. Chiara sees Lucia differently.
chapters.b_plot: Nadia reveals to Matteo that she had already applied for a job at a pharmacy in Milan before the baby. She had never told him.
chapters.arc: Chiara–Lucia: full respect. Nadia–Matteo tension planted.

title.en: I Can't Take It Any More

grammar.name: Pronominal verbs
grammar.scope: farcela, andarsene, cavarsela, prendersela, smetterla, sentirsela, metterci; forms in present and past (ce l'ho fatta, se n'è andato)

chapters.a_plot: Ben, alone all week with the kids, the bar and his business plan, finally cracks. He walks out of the house and ends up at Franco's orto at midnight.
chapters.b_plot: Franco, who never gives advice, gives Ben advice. It's about Anna, and it's good.

grammar.name: Fare + infinitive (causative)
grammar.scope: fare fare, far vedere, far sapere; farsi + infinitive (farsi tagliare i capelli); pronouns with causatives

chapters.theme: Services, getting things done: tailor, florist, hairdresser
chapters.a_plot: Franco has a suit made for the wedding by the tailor who made his first one, 45 years ago. He also has his hair cut for the first time in a salon.
chapters.b_plot: Lucia has everything done for her by professionals, except the wedding cake, which she makes herself and lets nobody see.
chapters.runner: Ben: 'Mi faccio fare un logo!' (Emma designs it for free.)

grammar.name: Uses of the gerund
grammar.scope: gerund for manner, means, cause and time (sbagliando s'impara, camminando, essendo stanco); pronouns attached (parlandone); subject rules

chapters.a_plot: Ben prepares his first cooking class for foreigners. How do you teach? He studies Alberto's methods, and his own mistakes as a learner.
chapters.b_plot: Emma tutors Leo for his Italian test, and discovers she's a good teacher (and that she's now more Italian than American).

grammar.name: Infinitive constructions
grammar.scope: prima di + infinitive; dopo + infinito passato (dopo aver mangiato, dopo essere arrivati); senza + infinitive; invece di + infinitive

chapters.theme: Cooking class, cooking verbs, food from around the world
chapters.a_plot: Ben's first cooking class for foreigners at Bar Tigli: a Japanese engineer, a German couple and an American exchange student. It's a huge success. Then, in the tag, a small fire.
chapters.b_plot: Franco watches from the door, pretending he's just passing by.
chapters.arc: TENTPOLE: Ben's first professional success in Italy.

grammar.name: Advanced comparisons
grammar.scope: più ... di quanto / di quello che; meglio vs migliore, peggio vs peggiore; sempre più / sempre meno; più ... più

chapters.a_plot: A new trendy café opens in the piazza with 'American brunch' and lower prices. Ben's classes and Matteo's bar face their first real competition.
chapters.b_plot: Emma and Tommaso compare everything: families, futures, music. 'Più ci penso, meno capisco.'
chapters.runner: The online reviews for Bar Tigli, read aloud by Matteo.

grammar.name: Impersonal si with reflexive verbs; si + adjectives
grammar.scope: ci si alza, ci si abitua; si è stanchi (plural adjective); impersonal si in compound tenses (si è mangiato bene)

chapters.theme: Work culture, adapting, Italian workplace habits
chapters.a_plot: Chiara in Rome is homesick for Borgoverde. In Rome people work differently, eat differently and speak differently. 'Ci si abitua,' says her Roman colleague.
chapters.b_plot: Ben's German students ask him how you get used to Italy. He gives a speech he didn't know he had in him.
chapters.arc: Chiara begins to question the Rome project.

grammar.name: Formal emails and letters
grammar.scope: formal openings and closings (Gentile..., Egregio..., Cordiali saluti, In attesa di un Suo riscontro); polite conditional; formal Lei in writing

chapters.a_plot: The mysterious stranger from E3 was a council inspector: the cooking classes need an authorisation. Ben must write formal emails, and Roberto (of all people) helps him.
chapters.b_plot: Emma writes a formal email to her headmistress asking for a summer exchange programme in Ireland.

grammar.name: Lasciare + infinitive; permettere di
grammar.scope: lasciare fare, lasciar perdere, lasciami stare; permettere di / vietare di; pronouns with lasciare

chapters.a_plot: Emma wants to spend the summer in Dublin on an exchange. Ben says 'lasciala andare'; Chiara, from Rome, says no.
chapters.b_plot: Franco lets Leo drive the old tractor at a friend's farm, without telling anyone. Chiara finds out.

grammar.name: Indirect questions
grammar.scope: mi chiedo se, non so cosa/chi/dove/come, dimmi perché; si vs se; indicative in indirect questions (the subjunctive comes later)

chapters.a_plot: Leo's First Communion, which Franco insisted on. Ben and Chiara aren't sure what they believe; Leo has many questions for Don Luigi.
chapters.b_plot: The Communion lunch: 40 people and six courses. Samira brings food for 80.
chapters.arc: TENTPOLE: the whole ensemble; Franco's joy.

grammar.name: Adjectives and nouns + prepositions
grammar.scope: contento di, capace di, pronto a, abituato a, stanco di, interessato a, bravo a/in, la voglia di, il bisogno di

chapters.a_plot: Tommaso is accepted into a summer music course in Siena. Emma is proud of him and jealous of him; she has nothing of her own yet.
chapters.b_plot: Matteo is 'stanco di' being the one who doesn't finish things. He challenges himself to complete one project: the bar's new terrace.
chapters.runner: Ornella: 'Sono orgogliosa di te,' to Ben. He writes it in his notebook.

grammar.name: Word formation: prefixes and suffixes
grammar.scope: prefixes ri-, s-, dis-, in-/im-; noun suffixes -zione, -mento, -tore/-trice, -ista, -ezza, -ità; forming words from verbs and adjectives

chapters.theme: Jobs and professions; building and making
chapters.a_plot: Matteo's terrace project goes wrong: he has to redo everything, and discovers he likes building. His father the tram driver was a builder too, before the trams.
chapters.b_plot: Nadia is offered the job in Milan she had applied for (S4E8). She has to decide: stay at Farmacia Centrale or become the 'direttrice' of a new pharmacy.

title.en: It Costs an Arm and a Leg

grammar.name: Idioms with the body
grammar.scope: costare un occhio della testa, avere le mani bucate, in bocca al lupo, avere la testa fra le nuvole, a occhio e croce, non chiudere occhio, essere in gamba, prendere in giro

chapters.a_plot: The wedding budget explodes. Lucia has 'le mani bucate'; Franco has 'il braccino corto' (he's stingy). Chiara, from Rome, takes over the spreadsheet.
chapters.b_plot: Leo collects idioms in a notebook, like his father, and uses them all at the wrong moments.
chapters.runner: Ben translates idioms literally for his students, with disastrous results.

grammar.name: Colloquial dislocation
grammar.scope: left dislocation with resumptive pronoun (il caffè lo prendo io, a Marco gli ho detto...); right dislocation (lo so, che hai ragione); ne and ci in dislocation

chapters.a_plot: Chiara returns from Rome to a house that functions perfectly without her. Who does what? She feels useless, the way Ben felt in S1.
chapters.b_plot: Lucia and Franco divide the chores in their house. Franco has never ironed in his life.
chapters.arc: Chiara decides to cut back on Rome.

grammar.name: Conjunctions with the indicative
grammar.scope: anche se, dato che, poiché, visto che, mentre (contrast), eppure, comunque, dal momento che; linking reasons and contrasts

chapters.a_plot: Emma leaves for Dublin, 'anche se' Chiara isn't ready. At Malpensa airport, the whole family, and Tommaso, who's leaving for Siena the next day.
chapters.b_plot: Ben finds Emma's old notebook: songs about Chicago, then Borgoverde, then Tommaso.

grammar.name: Future and present for the future; forecasts
grammar.scope: future vs present for scheduled events; the weather forecast language (previsioni: pioverà, ci saranno temporali, temperature in aumento)

chapters.theme: Weather forecasts, summer storms, contingency plans
chapters.a_plot: One week before the outdoor wedding, the forecast says storms. Franco checks the forecast 40 times a day. Ben and Roberto build a plan B together.
chapters.b_plot: Gennaro and Chiara plan a surprise for the reception: a video with Anna's and Lucia's old photos from the dance class.
chapters.runner: Ornella predicts the weather from her knee. She's more accurate than the app.

grammar.name: Structuring a speech
grammar.scope: innanzitutto, in primo luogo, inoltre, oltre a, per quanto riguarda, infine, per concludere; addressing an audience

chapters.a_plot: Franco asks Ben to be his best man. Ben must write the speech in Italian, the most important Italian text of his life so far.
chapters.b_plot: Emma, back early from Dublin for the wedding, helps him write it, and cuts all his jokes.
chapters.arc: Ben as Franco's testimone: full acceptance.

grammar.name: Review: future, conditional, pronouns
grammar.scope: Consolidation of futuro semplice/anteriore, condizionale presente/passato, combined and pronominal forms, relative pronouns, speech structure

chapters.a_plot: The wedding at San Vittore and the reception in the orto. Storm clouds, then sun. Ben's speech, the video of Anna and Lucia, and the first dance: a tango.
chapters.b_plot: Nadia tells Matteo her decision about the Milan job (open ending for S5). Emma and Tommaso dance by the hedge.
chapters.arc: SEASON FINALE: Franco and Lucia are married.
